candidates.text:
Business Requirement:
1. Operation Cost Templates cannot be tagged to a specific factory, which prevents factory-specific costing.
2. A cost template supports only a single cost component, with no ability to separate costs by operation type (Regular, PCS Rate, Idle, OT).
3. SAM, Qty per Hour, and process cost are not auto-calculated on the Routing page, requiring manual entry and increasing the risk of error.
4. The system does not support maintaining different process costs for the same process across different colours, forcing users to create duplicate routings.
5. The Master Costsheet does not provide fields to capture additional charges (e.g., Freight Cost) against Fabric and Trims line items.
candidates.locator: § Business Requirement

candidates.text: The enhancements described in this document are intended to remove these limitations.
candidates.locator: § Business Requirement

Proposed Enhancement:
1. Add a Factory selection field to the Operation Cost Template Master screen.
2. Each cost template can be tagged to one particular factory at the time of creation or edit.
3. Once tagged, the template becomes specific to that factory and should be usable wherever that factory is selected in routing.

candidates.text:
Standard Operating Procedure / Business Rule:
1. The system distinguishes between "Global Factory" (used for Costsheet/budget) and "Actual Factory" (used to calculate actual production cost).
2. Global factory setup: The Shahi team will create one Global Factory per division, named accordingly — e.g., Shahi Exports Pvt Ltd-MNB, Shahi Exports Pvt Ltd-LSD, etc.
3. Usage in costing: These Global Factories are used to calculate the budget in the Costsheet. Users select the Global Factory in Routing, and the system calculates the total cost based on the cost template mapped to that factory.

chunks.title: Purpose
chunks.heading: Purpose
chunks.text: Need some enhancements in BOM Routing.
chunks.locator: § Purpose

chunks.title: Business Requirement
chunks.heading: Business Requirement
chunks.text:
The current BOM Routing and Operation Cost Template functionality has the following limitations that this specification addresses:
• Operation Cost Templates cannot be tagged to a specific factory, which prevents factory-specific costing.
• A cost template supports only a single cost component, with no ability to separate costs by operation type (Regular, PCS Rate, Idle, OT).
• SAM, Qty per Hour, and process cost are not auto-calculated on the Routing page, requiring manual entry and increasing the risk of error.
• The system does not support maintaining different process costs for the same process across different colours, forcing users to create duplicate routings.
• The Master Costsheet does not provide fields to capture additional charges (e.g., Freight Cost) against Fabric and Trims line items.
The enhancements described in this document are intended to remove these limitations.
chunks.locator: § Business Requirement

chunks.title: Current Behaviour
chunks.heading: Changes in Operation Cost Templates. › … › 3.1.1 Addition of Factory in Operation Cost Template Master › Current Behaviour
chunks.text:
• Users can create an Operation Cost Template, but the template cannot be tagged to a particular factory.
• As a result, the same template applies system-wide and cannot reflect factory-specific cost differences.
Figure 1: Current Screen — Operation Cost Template Master (no factory field)
chunks.locator: § Changes in Operation Cost Templates. › … › 3.1.1 Addition of Factory in Operation Cost Template Master › Current Behaviour

chunks.title: Proposed Enhancement
chunks.heading: Changes in Operation Cost Templates. › … › 3.1.1 Addition of Factory in Operation Cost Template Master › Proposed Enhancement
chunks.text:
• Add a Factory selection field to the Operation Cost Template Master screen.
• Each cost template can be tagged to one particular factory at the time of creation or edit.
• Once tagged, the template becomes specific to that factory and should be usable wherever that factory is selected in routing.
Figure 2: Proposed Screen — Operation Cost Template Master with Factory field
chunks.locator: § Changes in Operation Cost Templates. › … › 3.1.1 Addition of Factory in Operation Cost Template Master › Proposed Enhancement

chunks.title: Standard Operating Procedure / Business Rule
chunks.heading: Changes in Operation Cost Templates. › … › 3.1.1 Addition of Factory in Operation Cost Template Master › Standard Operating Procedure / Business Rule
chunks.text:
• The system distinguishes between "Global Factory" (used for Costsheet/budget) and "Actual Factory" (used to calculate actual production cost).
• Global factory setup: The Shahi team will create one Global Factory per division, named accordingly — e.g., Shahi Exports Pvt Ltd-MNB, Shahi Exports Pvt Ltd-LSD, etc.
• Usage in costing: These Global Factories are used to calculate the budget in the Costsheet. Users select the Global Factory in Routing, and the system calculates the total cost based on the cost template mapped to that factory.
Note: Global Factory drives budgeted/Costsheet cost; the Actual Factory continues to be used to compute the actual in-production cost.
chunks.locator: § Changes in Operation Cost Templates. › … › 3.1.1 Addition of Factory in Operation Cost Template Master › Standard Operating Procedure / Business Rule

chunks.title: Current Behaviour
chunks.heading: Changes in Operation Cost Templates. › … › 3.1.2 Addition of Sections in Cost Component › Current Behaviour
chunks.text:
• A cost template supports attaching only a single cost component.
• There is no way to differentiate cost by operation section such as Regular, PCS Rate, Idle, or OT within the same template.
Figure 3: Current Screen — single cost component, no section bifurcation
chunks.locator: § Changes in Operation Cost Templates. › … › 3.1.2 Addition of Sections in Cost Component › Current Behaviour

chunks.title: Proposed Enhancement
chunks.heading: Changes in Operation Cost Templates. › … › 3.1.2 Addition of Sections in Cost Component › Proposed Enhancement
chunks.text:
• Introduce distinct Sections within a single cost template: Regular, PCS Rate, Idle, and OT.
• Each section can carry its own cost component and its own validity period, independent of the other sections.
Figure 4: Proposed Screen — cost template with sections
• On the "Cost Values" screen, the system will first display the available sections; each section then shows its own cost component and validity.
Figure 5: Cost Values screen — sections with cost component and validity
• Users can copy a cost component from one section to another within the same template, to avoid re-entering identical values.
Figure 6: Copy Cost Component option across sections
• Once user selects the Cost template in routing then system picks the value of the “Regular Section” of this cost template.
chunks.locator: § Changes in Operation Cost Templates. › … › 3.1.2 Addition of Sections in Cost Component › Proposed Enhancement

chunks.title: 3.1.3 Routing Page — SAM Calculation Workflow
chunks.heading: Changes in Operation Cost Templates. › … › 3.1.3 Routing Page — SAM Calculation Workflow
chunks.text:
We required a new field in Routing as Effective SAM whose calculation will be based on below steps:-
• Step 1: The user selects the Factory. The Cost of Sub Operation per minute is fetched automatically based on this selection.
• Step 2: The user enters the Efficiency percentage in the Efficiency column.
• Step 3: The user enters the Production Time.
• Step 4: An additional field, SAM, is auto-calculated as Production Time × Efficiency percentage — the user does not enter this value manually.
Figure 7: Routing page — Sub Operation Cost, Efficiency, Production Time, and auto-calculated SAM
chunks.locator: § Changes in Operation Cost Templates. › … › 3.1.3 Routing Page — SAM Calculation Workflow

chunks.title: 3.1.4 Additional Fields on the Routing Page
chunks.heading: Changes in Operation Cost Templates. › … › 3.1.4 Additional Fields on the Routing Page
chunks.text:
The following extra fields are required on the Routing page:
Figure 8: Routing page with extra fields highlighted
• 1. Qty per Hour: Auto-calculated as 60 / SAM. Example: if SAM = 30, Qty per Hour = 60 / 30 = 2.
• 2. No of Stitches: Entered manually by the user.
Note: A process can be added to the routing without filling these fields, since some processes (e.g., Packing) do not require this data.

chunks.title: 3.2 Colour-wise Process Cost in Routing
chunks.heading: Changes in Operation Cost Templates. › 3.2 Colour-wise Process Cost in Routing
chunks.text: Requirement 2: The system should provide an option in Routing Creation to maintain separate process costs colour-wise for the same routing process.
chunks.locator: § Changes in Operation Cost Templates. › 3.2 Colour-wise Process Cost in Routing

chunks.title: Objective
chunks.heading: Changes in Operation Cost Templates. › 3.2 Colour-wise Process Cost in Routing › … › Objective
chunks.text: To allow users to maintain different process costs for different colours within the same routing, without duplicating the routing itself.
chunks.locator: § Changes in Operation Cost Templates. › 3.2 Colour-wise Process Cost in Routing › … › Objective

chunks.title: Existing Scenario
chunks.heading: Changes in Operation Cost Templates. › 3.2 Colour-wise Process Cost in Routing › … › Existing Scenario
chunks.text:
For example, during routing creation there is a process named "Bleach". The Bleach process itself remains the same, but its cost can vary depending on colour:
• Black Colour → Bleach Cost = 10
• White Colour → Bleach Cost = 12
• Red Colour → Bleach Cost = 8
Currently, the system allows only one common cost for a process irrespective of colour. If a user wants different prices per colour, they must create a separate routing per colour.
Figure 9: Existing routing screen — single cost per process, irrespective of colour
chunks.locator: § Changes in Operation Cost Templates. › 3.2 Colour-wise Process Cost in Routing › … › Existing Scenario

chunks.title: Requirement
chunks.heading: Changes in Operation Cost Templates. › 3.2 Colour-wise Process Cost in Routing › … › Requirement
chunks.text:
• Provide an option in Routing Creation to enter separate process costs colour-wise for the same routing process.
• The system should support maintaining different costs for different colours without requiring creation of multiple routings for the same process.
• Here need to open a window which will allow to put cost at color level.
• When user click on Add color then dropdown will also have an option of All colors.
• Same window to update cost color wise is required on Billing on Input as well.
• Higher cost to be included in Add to cost.
• If this BOM is used as a manufacturing BOM, then system should pick the process cost as per the material color used for the material line. In case multiple colors are mapped then system will take the higher cost.
chunks.locator: § Changes in Operation Cost Templates. › 3.2 Colour-wise Process Cost in Routing › … › Requirement

chunks.title: 3.3 Changes in Master Costsheet
chunks.heading: Changes in Operation Cost Templates. › 3.3 Changes in Master Costsheet
chunks.text:
Requirement: Need Additional Charges fields in the Fabric and Trims Detail Table present in the Master Costsheet.
Figure 10: Master Costsheet — Fabric and Trims Detail Table
Clicking the relevant button on this screen opens the Additional Charges entry screen shown below and same to be included in Cost/gmt, total, total (in lac) and % of realization.
Figure 11: Additional Charges entry screen (e.g., Freight Cost)
This table needs fields for additional charges such as Freight Cost.
Note: Add these fields after "Section Total" so that the additional charges are added to the Section Total, after which the system displays the "Grand Total".
